description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of a multimodal misinformation detection model across two datasets — PHEME and PolitiFact — under various ablation conditions, as presented in the paper “Bridging Cognition and Emotion: Empathy-Driven Multimodal Misinformation Detection.” The vertical axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 75.0% to 95.0% in increments of 2.5%, while the horizontal axis lists six experimental conditions: “Ours” (the full model), “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition.” The chart is divided into two panels: the left panel for PHEME and the right for PolitiFact. In PHEME, the full model (“Ours”) achieves 89.84% accuracy, followed by “w/o select” at 88.80%, “w/o emotion” at 87.34%, “w/o cognition” at 87.17%, “w/o comments” at 86.82%, and “w/o text” at 80.10%. In PolitiFact, “Ours” reaches 90.57%, “w/o select” 89.62%, “w/o cognition” 87.74%, “w/o emotion” 84.91%, “w/o comments” 85.85%, and “w/o text” 83.02%. Across both datasets, removing text input causes the most significant drop in performance, while the full model consistently outperforms all ablated variants, underscoring the importance of integrating textual, emotional, and cognitive signals for effective misinformation detection.
